subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw define execution anti-drift as a core durable run-state contract, and what artifact, timer, persistence, feature-flag, telemetry, and post-green semantics should it enforce?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the proposed fix chooses product-visible runtime semantics, persisted state ownership, config/flag shape, escalation behavior, and overlap with existing diagnostic/heartbeat/watchdog systems.

options.title: Design Core Contract First
options.body: Define the artifact set, state owner, timer defaults, escalation cooldowns, telemetry schema, post-green behavior, and compatibility expectations before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Existing Surfaces
options.body: Extend current diagnostics, heartbeat responses, loop detection, cron watchdogs, and subagent lifecycle paths without creating a separate run-state authority.

options.title: Narrow To Watchdog Only
options.body: Keep this broad issue as design guidance but implement only a smaller accepted-task/progress watchdog through the narrower related issue.

recommendation.title: Design Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Define the artifact set, state owner, timer defaults, escalation cooldowns, telemetry schema, post-green behavior, and compatibility expectations before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the broadest inspected history across diagnostics, subagent lifecycle, heartbeat, and runtime maintenance, making him the best available owner for the contract decision.
